title: Six Weeks Behind
genre: psychedelic folk (Incredible String Band lineage, acoustic, droney)
subject: two pen pals since age eleven, one on Orkney and one in Tasmania, whose letters take six weeks each way so each answers a question the other asked in another season
caption: Psychedelic folk in the 1967 Incredible String Band tradition. Fingerpicked steel-string acoustic guitar in open tuning, hammered dulcimer ringing over a tanpura drone, wooden flute with a breathy tone, hand drums and finger cymbals keeping a loose lilting pulse. Warm room recording, light tape echo on the dulcimer, organic and slightly ragged. Male and female voices trading lines and joining in unison, clearly sung with a folk lilt. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 96 BPM, D dorian. Dreamy, playful, wistful mood. No electric guitar, no synthesizer, no drum kit, no autotune, no rap.
lyrics:
[Intro - dulcimer, drone and flute]

[Verse 1]
You sent me a question in the middle of June
I opened it when the first snow came down
You asked if the lambs had come early this year
I said yes, and they're sheep now

[Pre-Chorus]
Your winter is my summer
My morning is your night

[Chorus]
Six weeks behind, six weeks behind
Over the water, we talk
I answer you now what you asked me before
And you'll answer me back in the autumn

[Verse 2]
Your letter smelled faintly of eucalyptus
Mine smelled of peat smoke and rain
You said you'd been sick and you're better again
I wrote, get well soon, by the way

[Pre-Chorus]
We've been at it since eleven
Two grey heads on two thin pages

[Bridge - flute and drone alone]
If I ever stand on your shore
Will you know me by my handwriting

[Chorus]
Six weeks behind, six weeks behind
The ink is still wet on my thumb
I answer you now what you asked me before
And you'll answer me back in the autumn

[Outro - dulcimer and flute fade]
